name: Terraria
short: Invasions, blood moons, buffs, items, slaps and fireworks through a TShock server
description: You run a TShock server (the free, open-source Terraria server) on this PC and join it from Terraria. GiftDeck sends commands to TShock's REST API, so gifts start invasions, blood moons, eclipses and slime rain, give items, boss summons and coins, buff or debuff your character, slap you, launch fireworks, change the time and weather, and more.
warning: Commands go through TShock's REST API, and TShock only lets in-game players use /spawnmob, /spawnboss, /item, /buff and /tp. So gifts can't drop a single mob or boss on you; enemies come from invasions, moons, eclipses and slime rain, and boss summon items are given to you to use.

requirements.detail: Your Terraria version must match the TShock version. TShock's download page says which Terraria version each release is for. If Steam updates Terraria first, wait for the matching TShock release.
The free Terraria server from github.com/Pryaxis/TShock. Download the win-x64 zip from the latest release.
TShock is built on .NET 9. If TShock.Server.exe says .NET is missing, install the .NET 9 Runtime from Microsoft.

requirements.text: A REST token in TShock's config.json
requirements.detail: The guide below shows the three lines to add. The token is the password GiftDeck uses.

guide.title: Download TShock
guide.text: Download the latest TShock release for Windows (the file ending in win-x64-Release.zip) and unzip it into a folder of its own, for example C:\TShock. Don't put it in Program Files. Check that the release says it's for the same Terraria version you have (Terraria's title screen shows your version in the corner). TShock needs the .NET 9 Runtime (x64); install it from Microsoft if TShock says it's missing.

guide.title: Start the server once and make a world
guide.text: Double-click TShock.Server.exe. A console window opens and asks you to choose a world: type n and press Enter to make a new one, then answer the questions (size, difficulty, name). Press Enter to keep the default port 7777 and no password. When the world has loaded, type off in the console and press Enter. This saves the world and closes the server. On that first run TShock also created a tshock folder next to TShock.Server.exe.

guide.title: Turn on the REST API and make a token
Start the server and join it
guide.text: Start TShock.Server.exe again and pick your world (type its number). In Terraria: Multiplayer > Join via IP, pick your character, type 127.0.0.1 as the address and 7777 as the port. Keep the server window open while you stream.

guide.title: Connect GiftDeck
guide.text: On this page type host 127.0.0.1, port 7878, your REST token as the password, and your character's name exactly as it shows in game. Press Test: GiftDeck asks TShock who is online. If it says the token isn't valid, check the token in config.json and restart TShock.

guide.title: Add gift events
guide.text: In an event, add the action "Run a game command" and pick a Terraria command, for example a blood moon for a big gift or a firework for a Rose. Messages in game say that "GiftDeck" did it (the Username from your token). Blood moon, eclipse, rain, slime rain, sandstorm, god mode and lanterns switch on and off, so the same gift twice turns them off again. Starting an invasion while one is running ends it instead.
